identity.title: FLIP2: Expanding Protein Fitness Landscape Benchmarks for Real-World Machine Learning Applications

problem.claim: Protein-fitness predictors remain sensitive to distribution shifts, raising questions about their practical utility for protein engineering.

gap.claim: The FLIP benchmark covered only stability, binding, and viral-capsid viability, with limited coverage of engineering-relevant domains and shifts.

contributions.claim: Introduces FLIP2, spanning seven new protein-fitness datasets and splits intended to measure generalization relevant to real-world engineering campaigns.
Reports evaluations of benchmark models across the new datasets and suites, including comparisons between simpler models and fine-tuned protein language models.
Records dataset provenance and redistributes all data under CC-BY 4.0.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish FLIP2 by adding seven datasets—including enzymes, protein-protein interactions, and light-sensitive proteins—and real-world-relevant generalization splits.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that simpler models often matched or outperformed fine-tuned protein language models on FLIP2.
The authors report that these results challenge the utility of existing transfer-learning techniques.

narrative_sequence.summary: Distribution sensitivity limits generalization and leaves protein engineers uncertain about ML utility.
FLIP tested some domain shifts but was restricted to three measurement categories.
FLIP2 expands coverage with seven datasets and engineering-relevant splits.
Model evaluations indicate that simpler models often perform at least as well as fine-tuned protein language models, challenging transfer-learning utility.
Dataset provenance is recorded and the data are redistributed under CC-BY 4.0.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links benchmark expansion to specific real-world generalization splits, then reports model comparisons across those suites.

lessons.interpretation: A benchmark claim is more informative when its task coverage and evaluation splits are explicitly tied to the deployment question.
lessons.application: Define benchmark splits around the intended operational shifts before comparing model classes.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when deployment shifts or representative datasets cannot be specified credibly.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the seven datasets, split definitions, metrics, model suite, or quantitative margins.
The reported comparison lacks conditions needed to determine when simpler models match or outperform fine-tuned language models.
